title: EMLIO: Minimizing I/O Latency and Energy Consumption for Large-Scale AI Training
problem: Large-scale deep learning training faces I/O bottlenecks as datasets exceed local storage and GPU compute outpaces network/disk latencies. While recent systems optimize data-loading time, energy consumption of I/O—critical at scale—is overlooked. Multi-environment networks (LAN/WAN) require different strategies.
motivation: I/O energy can dominate total energy budget in large-scale training. Current optimizations focus on latency alone. Need joint optimization of latency (T) and energy (E) that adapts to variable network distances without performance penalty.
method: EMLIO: Efficient ML I/O service. Deploys lightweight daemon on storage nodes that serializes/batches raw samples, streams over TCP with out-of-order prefetching. Integrates with GPU preprocessing (NVIDIA DALI) on client. Evaluates across local disk, LAN (0.05ms, 10ms RTT), WAN (30ms RTT).
key_novelty: First end-to-end optimization framework jointly minimizing I/O latency and energy consumption; maintains constant performance/energy profiles across variable network distances.
contributions: Storage daemon with sample batching and serialization
TCP streaming with out-of-order prefetch strategy
Integration with NVIDIA DALI for GPU preprocessing

metrics.consistency: Constant performance and energy profiles regardless of network distance

limitations: Abstract only - no specific benchmarks, no breakdown by dataset size/type, no comparison with other distributed I/O frameworks
primary_theme: Energy-aware I/O for distributed AI training
